dossier.public_summary: The signal does not repeat consistently: odd and even dips differ by a factor of two and the five individual events range from nonexistent to twice as deep, with one negative dip. The star also shows strong, period-related brightness swings. Together this is best explained by a blended or stellar variability that mimics a transit when folded at 14.9 days, not a 2 Earth-sized transiting planet.

reasons.why: Strong odd-even difference (depth_odd_ppm 332.2 vs depth_even_ppm 716.5, ratio 2.2) points to an eclipsing binary folded at half the 14.9 d period, not a planet at 14.9 d.
Individual transits are wildly inconsistent: p_consistent essentially zero and share_of_top_3 0.907 with one deep (816 ppm) and one negative (-57 ppm) event, opposite of a stable planet transit.

Large out-of-eclipse swing (amplitude_ppm 96.74, ratio_to_depth 0.2012, chi2 33.61, dof 9) on a star with rotation_d 5.808 and amplitude_ppm 2535-4786 ppm indicates spot/close-binary variability, not a flat planet phase curve.

Apparent depth changes between sectors 35, 62 and 89 support the inconsistent-depth/variability picture; sector_depths_by_source says steady within source but the folding-period artefact already explains the variation.
